status_summary: EO 14251 (signed 2025-03-27) excluded USCIS, ICE, CISA, FEMA and the Coast Guard, along with several DHS headquarters offices, from the federal labor-relations statute; it does not list TSA or CBP, and USCIS and FEMA were reported in August 2025 to have cancelled their union contracts. For TSA, DHS announced on 2025-03-07 that it was ending collective bargaining for about 47,000 screeners, but the Western District of Washington enjoined the Secretary's determination on 2025-06-02 and, on 2026-01-15, enforced that injunction against a second determination issued in September 2025, holding that the 2024 agreement remained binding. A three-day bench trial had been set for 2026-09-14, but on 2026-05-11 the court suspended the dispositive-motion deadline and asked the parties to propose new deadlines, and no later docket entry was found. The government-wide order and its litigation are covered in c03-02 and are not restated here.

timeline.event: DHS announced it was ending collective bargaining for about 47,000 TSA screeners, following a determination by the Secretary dated 2025-02-27.

EO 14251 signed (90 FR 14553, published 2025-04-03); section 2 adds to EO 12171 a list of DHS subdivisions excluded from the federal labor-relations program (pp. 14553-14554): Office of the Secretary, General Counsel, Strategy Policy and Plans, Management Directorate, Science and Technology, Health Security, Situational Awareness, USCIS, ICE, Coast Guard, CISA and FEMA. TSA and CBP are not listed.
The Western District of Washington (AFGE v. Noem) granted a preliminary injunction barring implementation of the TSA determination.
The court denied the government's first motion to dismiss in AFGE v. Noem (ECF 47).
Reports said USCIS had told unions it would cancel its collective bargaining agreements and that FEMA had ended its agreements, following EO 14251 and an early August appeals court decision.
The Secretary issued a second TSA determination, whose implementation date was later extended to 2026-01-18.
The court granted AFGE's motion to enforce, ruling that the September determination could not take effect and that the 2024 agreement remained binding.

The court granted a stipulated motion suspending the 2026-05-18 dispositive-motion deadline and ordered a joint status report by 2026-05-22 to reset remaining deadlines; the 2026-09-14 trial date was not shown as reset.
